Translation-Invariant Sparse KL-UOT

Source: R/uot_ti.R
ot_sinkhorn_unbalanced_ti.Rd

Solves finite-measure entropic unbalanced optimal transport with generalized KL penalties and translation-invariant Sinkhorn updates. Dense costs use complete support. Sparse costs may be a Matrix::sparseMatrix (structural nonzeros are the support), a 1-based source,target,cost edge list, or the CSR list used by manifoldalign. Edge-list shapes are supplied with n_source and n_target or embedded in the list.

Usage

ot_sinkhorn_unbalanced_ti(
  cost,
  p = NULL,
  q = NULL,
  epsilon = 0.05,
  rho = 10,
  max_iter = 2000L,
  tol = 1e-08,
  n_source = NULL,
  n_target = NULL,
  plan = c("operator", "sparse", "dense")
)

Arguments

cost

Dense matrix, sparse Matrix, edge list, or CSR sparse-cost list.

p, q

Finite nonnegative source and target measures. Defaults are probability measures; positive total mass is required.

epsilon

Positive entropic regularization.

rho

One or two positive marginal KL penalties.

max_iter

Maximum TI-Sinkhorn iterations.

tol

Positive iterate tolerance. Independent KKT, fixed-point, and primal-dual tolerances are derived and reported.

n_source, n_target

Sparse edge-list shape; ignored for matrix costs.

plan

Returned plan representation: coupling-free "operator", explicit "sparse" edge plan, or explicitly allocated "dense" matrix.

Value

An rfugw_result with potentials, sparse-support diagnostics, objective components, KKT and primal-dual certificates, mass diagnostics, plan/operator representation, and runtime provenance.

Details

The optimized objective is $$\langle C, \pi\rangle + \rho_1 KL(\pi_1|p) + \rho_2 KL(\pi_2|q) + \epsilon KL(\pi|p\otimes q).$$ KL terms use finite-measure generalized KL, with the product-reference constant retained even outside sparse support. Potentials are returned in a canonical translated gauge. The plan is implicit by default, so apply and adjoint operations do not require dense materialization.

Examples

cost <- matrix(c(0, 1, 1, 0), 2)
fit <- ot_sinkhorn_unbalanced_ti(
  cost, p = c(2, 1), q = c(1, 3), epsilon = 0.2, rho = c(2, 3)
)
transport_plan_adjoint(rfugw_plan(fit), c(10, 20))
#> [1] 10.44277 39.02712
